chapter_theme: The vision of the holy dance: Siva dances everywhere and as everything, with Shakti, at Tillai and beyond all worlds, and his dancing sets the scriptures, the elements, the worlds and the mind dancing. The same dance is placed in the body, in the central channel, between the brows and in the heart, is read off the dancer's hands as the five acts and the five letters, and is known by its effects on those who see it: tears, melting, the end of self, and bliss.
structure_note: The chapter has no strict order but returns to a few strands: the dance as all-pervading bliss and play (2722 to 2731, 2786 to 2792); its cosmic and sacred places, Tillai and the south (2732, 2746, 2749, 2755, 2758, 2773 to 2775); its place in the yogic body, mapped onto Meru, Lanka and the Himalaya (2735, 2736, 2747, 2748, 2754, 2764, 2770, 2771); the dancer's attributes, hands and feet read as the five acts and the five letters (2780, 2781, 2797 to 2799); and its effect on the devotee who sees it (2740 to 2745, 2760, 2778, 2779, 2796). Many verses in the second half are numerical or compressed.

2722.reading: Everywhere is his holy form, everywhere Siva and Shakti, everywhere Chidambaram, everywhere the holy dance; because Siva is everywhere, the grace of Siva that abides everywhere is his own play.
2722.nuance: The verse opens the chapter by freeing the dance from one place: Chidambaram and the dance are wherever Siva is. விளையாட்டு (play) names the whole of his grace as sport, the idea tradition calls lila.

2723.reading: Who can know the dancer of Siva's bliss, the supreme light of consciousness, the beautiful dancer who is the state of the word, the dancer of the golden city, of golden Tillai, the wondrous dancer?
2723.nuance: சொற்பதம் (the word-state) may be the state reached through words or the one beyond them; the verse does not settle it. பொற்பதி and பொன்தில்லை both name Chidambaram's golden hall.

2724.reading: See the great dance of bliss, streaming honey, above the endless Shakti of eternal bliss; for the Lord who dances beyond knowledge, she became the stage for his dance of bliss.
2724.nuance: Shakti is the stage (ஆடரங்கு) and Siva the dancer: the pair is figured as dance and floor. ஞானம் கடந்து says the dance lies beyond knowledge, even liberating knowledge. தான்அந்தம் இல்லா (without end) returns as wordplay in 2796.

2725.reading: For the one who delights in the dance of bliss, the stage is bliss, the songs are bliss, the instruments and their music are bliss, and the whole world of moving and unmoving things is bliss.

2726.reading: Light, the Supreme, the Supreme that is, the Supreme of gracious Sivakami and of the joy of the creeds: the clarity that is reached in contemplation is the attainment of the dance of Siva's bliss.
2726.nuance: Lines 2 and 3 are broken in syntax (சமயக் களியார் பரமும் கருதுறை யந்தக்), and the reading here only joins what can be joined. சிவகாமி is the name of the goddess at Chidambaram.

2727.reading: The dances are five; the one who is without form and with form dances them as the five acts, and by grace doing the five acts, the consort of her of honeyed speech dances the holy dance.
2727.nuance: அகள சகளத்தர் (the formless and formed one) is Siddhanta's term for Siva as both. The five dances are matched to the five acts, which 2799 assigns one by one to parts of the dancer's body. தேன்மொழி பாகன் is Siva as sharing his body with Uma.

2728.reading: The worlds of the elements, of distinction, of enjoyment, of yoga, of the ancients, of release, of delusion, of the body, of thirst and of the five acts: beyond them, in the Supreme, is the solitary great Brahmanda, they say.
2728.nuance: The verse is a list of compounds in -அண்டம் whose sense is mostly guessable from their first parts; தாகாண்ட (of thirst?) and the exact force of each are uncertain. The dance is not named; the verse sets the scale for the cosmic dance of the chapter.

2729.reading: The Vedas dance, the great Agamas dance, songs dance, the seven bright worlds dance, the elements dance, the whole world dances: with nada he danced the dance at the end of knowledge.
2729.nuance: His dance sets everything else dancing; the verb ஆட runs through the verse as a refrain, and 2751, 2756, 2789 and 2791 repeat the pattern. ஞானாந்தக் கூத்து (the dance at knowledge's end) sits beside நாதாந்தம் in 2751 as names for where the dance is.

2730.reading: The Siddha dances joined with the five elements, the senses, the five sense-objects, the five Vedas, the great Agama, the kalas that are recited, time and the aeons, and the five knowledges of the worlds.
2730.nuance: வேதங்கள் ஐந்து (five Vedas) is unusual, and அண்டப் போதங்கள் ஐந்து (five knowledges of the worlds) is obscure; both may follow the verse's run of fives rather than a fixed list. சித்தன் here names Siva.

2731.reading: Gods, suras, men, siddhas, vidyadharas, the three, the thirty-three from the beginning, ascetics, Shaktas, the creeds and all moving and unmoving things dance as our Lord dances.
2731.nuance: The creeds (சமயம்) are listed among the dancers: whatever their differences, they move by his movement.

2732.reading: Beyond and beyond the seven worlds, above the crown of Shakti and Sadasiva who are said to be there, the dark-throated one took a holy form of compassion and delighted in the dance there for Uma to see.
2732.nuance: The dance is placed above even Sadasiva, the highest form in the usual Siddhanta ordering, and is done so that Uma may watch: the dance as a form taken out of compassion (கருணை திருவுரு).

2733.reading: Kodukotti, Pandarangam, Kodu and Samharam, dances eight, and five and six sought within the nadis; firm and seven; the deodar forest, Tillai and the great banyan forest: he is the king of these.
2733.nuance: கொடுகொட்டி, பாண்டரங்கம் and சங்காரம் are traditionally names of Siva's dances, known also from the Silappatikaram; தேவதாரு, தில்லை and வடம் (the banyan, taken as Tiruvalangadu) are traditionally places of his dance. The numbers and the syntax of lines 2 and 3 are unclear.

2734.reading: Within the supreme cosmos are the feet of Parashakti, within it the Lord of spreading light, within it the spreading nada, and within it the Supreme dances.

2735.reading: With the path that rises like a goad in awakening and the beat of the rhythm called thonthi, Sankara dances held within the root nadi; when that time swells, there is no entering and no going.
2735.nuance: அங்குசம் (goad), தொந்தி and மூலநாடி are yogic terms whose exact sense is not fixed by the verse; தொந்தி may be a rhythm term or a name for a bodily centre. புகும் போகல் இல்லை is commonly taken as the breath's coming and going ceasing, and may also be read as an end of birth and death.

2736.reading: My Lord danced as Nandi, then danced the new (or nine) dances, danced as Nandi of the forest, held it in thought and danced, danced within the threefold sushumna, danced within endless knowledge, and completed it.
2736.nuance: ஆன்நந்தி and கான்நந்தி are obscure and may be wordplay on ஆனந்தம் (bliss); நவக் கூத்து is either new or nine dances. The verse traces the dance inward, from outer forms to the central channel and then to knowledge.

2737.reading: The five Shaktis, the five distinctions of Siva, the eight releases, the eight first states, the eight attainments, the eight states of Siva and the eight purities: the Lord dances his ancient dance through these.
2737.nuance: The sets of five and eight are named without their members, and the traditional lists cannot be checked against the verse.

2738.reading: The seven clouds, the seven islands of the wide sea, the bodies that surround them, the seven Siva-suns, the seven thirsts and the seven peaces: all that comes to be is contained beneath Nandi's feet.
2738.nuance: சிவபாற்கரன் (Siva-sun) and the sevens of thirst and peace are obscure. The point that holds is the last line: the whole ordered cosmos lies under the dancer's feet.

2739.reading: In the south, north, east, west and zenith, in the five wondrous faces, within the twofold pair of matchless great bliss, the Supreme stands and does his unique dance.
2739.nuance: The four directions and the zenith match the five faces of Sadasiva in Saiva iconography. உபய உபயம் (twofold of the twofold) is obscure; it may mean Siva and Shakti.

2740.reading: Those who reach his feet are his devotees; devotees are those who saw the dance in the golden hall; they are those who saw bliss at Hara's feet; those who have become devotees have received the Father's grace.
2740.nuance: The verse plays on அடி (foot) and அடியார் (devotee, one of the foot): to be a devotee is to have reached the feet, and the feet are those of the dancer.

2741.reading: Nandi, the dancer of good knowledge, subdued me who would not be subdued, set his foot on me, placed me in the place of supreme bliss, walked on, and settled deep within me as a picture.
2741.nuance: அடிவைத்து (placing the foot) is traditionally the guru's initiation by the feet. படம்தான் செய்து (making a picture, or a cloth, or a hood) is unclear; the image may be of the dancer imprinted within. இடம்காண் பரானநத்தத்தே looks garbled for பரானந்தத்தே (in supreme bliss).

2742.reading: The dancer in the heavens, the excellent dancer, the valiant dancer in the hall of red gold, the dancer of relationship, the dancer who is the Supreme: seeking him with joy, I placed him in my love.
2742.nuance: சம்பந்தக் கூத்தன் may mean the dancer who binds himself to souls; it could also allude to the saint Sambandar, which would be out of keeping with the rest of the list.

2743.reading: Who can describe the ruby dancer, the dancer of bountiful Tillai, the dancer with twisted locks in the adorned hall, the dancer of Siva's bliss in the far light, the dancer of pure gold?

2744.reading: Those who set their love on the beautiful golden flower-feet in the dance of the holy hall, perfect in its rightness, sob, tremble, fall, rise, grow faint in body, do not know themselves, and lose their cleverness.
2744.nuance: The signs are those of devotional rapture, and the corpus records a close parallel in the Tevaram. சதுர்கெடும் (cleverness is lost) presents the loss of composure as gain.

2745.reading: To see the drama, seeking ends, the mind's bewilderment ends, the breath in the body no longer withers, the senses that come through the intellect stop running, desire ends, and the gaze of bliss in the heart is held taut.
2745.nuance: வாட்டறும் கால் (the breath that no longer withers) and நாட்டம் முறுக்குறும் (the gaze is twisted tight) carry a yogic sense of stilled breath and fixed gaze. The verse can be read as the effects of seeing the dance or as the conditions for seeing it; காணவே allows both.

2746.reading: He danced with Kali, danced on the golden mountain, danced with the goblins, danced on the earth, danced amid water, fire, wind and the wide sky, and the Lord dances in the hall for all days.
2746.nuance: The dance with Kali is traditionally the contest at Tiruvalangadu, and கனகாசலம் (golden mountain) is Meru. The verse gathers the dance's mythic sites and ends with the hall, where it goes on.

2747.reading: Meru is the central nadi, ida and pingala are marked by the Himalaya of this sky and by Lanka, and sushumna rises through the Tillai forest and the cool Malaya: these are Siva's ground.
2747.nuance: The verse maps the body's channels onto the land: the central channel onto Meru and onto Tillai, the side channels onto places north and south. Which channel goes with which place is not clear in the text, and 2754 gives the scheme again. இவைசிவ பூமியே makes the yogic body itself holy ground.

2748.reading: South of Meru on the earth are, it is said, ida, pingala and the bright sushumna; the holy hall where the bearer of the half-moon dwells is the end of the boundary of the flawless world of the elements.
2748.nuance: Chidambaram, in the south, is set at the place matching sushumna; பூதாண்டத்து எல்லையின் ஈறு (the end of the boundary of the elemental world) places the hall at the limit of the material cosmos.

2749.reading: Taking the seven worlds as his golden city, the five ancient spaces as his city, and Shakti in the staff as his holy hall, the supreme light delighted in the dance.
2749.nuance: தெண்டு (staff) is taken here as தண்டு, the spine or central channel, as in 2771, which ends with the same line; then the hall is Shakti within the body's central staff. The five spaces (ஆகாசங்கள் ஐந்து) are a yogic list not given.

2750.reading: As a line of bliss and keen quality, filling the head with bliss and reaching the southern quarter, he became the enjoyer of bliss with his lady, passed beyond bliss, and danced.
2750.nuance: The compounds குரானந்த, சிரானந்தம், புரானந்த and நிரானந்த form a chain of bliss words whose first parts are unclear; குரானந்த may be குரு + ஆனந்தம். நிரானந்தம் (bliss beyond bliss, or no-bliss) is a known term for the state past bliss.

2751.reading: As the first Supreme dances, the fire in his palm dances, his celebrated matted hair dances, the datura dances, the half-moon dances, all above the earth and worlds dances: with nada he danced the dance at the end of nada.
2751.nuance: உன்மத்தம் is the datura flower Siva wears and also means frenzy; both senses may be in play. நாதாந்த நட்டம் puts the dance where sound itself ends.

2752.reading: The king's dance in the hall where we bow is the cosmic dance of the Lord of the sky; when one reaches Sivaloka, the true thing, the truth lies in the supreme silence at the end of knowledge.
2752.nuance: Line 4 (உம்பரம் மோனஞா ஞானந்தத்தில்) looks garbled; read as silence and ஞானாந்தம் (knowledge's end). The verse moves from the dance one bows to in the hall to a silence beyond it.

2753.reading: The worlds thrice seven, the seven spheres, the hundred and eight creeds that are means, nada with its end, the bliss of dance and the four states: with his half, the Supreme's two feet dance.
2753.nuance: The numbers are given without their members; நாற்பதம் may be the four states of release or the four paths. பாதியோடு (with the half) is taken as with Uma, who is half his body.

2754.reading: Ida and pingala are the Himalaya and Lanka, Meru standing in the middle is sushumna in the middle, and the Tillai forest one goes to is the root seen at hand, called the spreading one, the supreme of supremes.
2754.nuance: The mapping of 2747 again, more plainly: the side channels to the northern and southern limits, the central one to Meru and to Tillai. Lines 3 and 4 (கைகண்ட மூலம், படர்பொன்றி) are obscure.

2755.reading: With Kumari, the maiden at the land's end, the Kaveri, nine distinct holy waters and seven hills, and because the Vedas and Agamas, the great gain, were born there, the unchanging southern land is pure.
2755.nuance: A praise of the south, set among verses on the southern hall (2748, 2758). பிறத்தலான் (because born there) may claim that the Vedas and Agamas were revealed in the south, which tradition says of the Agamas; it may also mean that they flourish there.

2756.reading: Dancing in nada, dancing in the four states, dancing in the Veda, dancing above the end of fire, dancing in knowledge, the flawless Lord of the gods dances through the whole world.
2756.nuance: நாற்பதம் (the four states) and தழல் அந்தம் (fire's end) are technical and unglossed.

2757.reading: Dancing with the gods, dancing in the holy hall, dancing with the three, dancing with the company of sages, dancing within verse, dancing in Parashakti, the Lord of the dance dances within the king.
2757.nuance: கோவினுள் (within the king) may mean within the ruler, within the soul as lord of the body, or within the cow (the soul as பசு); the verse does not say.

2758.reading: In the southern holy hall the great one shines without difference, as those who have come to clarity know him: the one who says 'I am lord over the six faces' and 'I am the supreme guru of the declared creeds'.
2758.nuance: ஆறு முகம் (six faces) is commonly taken as the six creeds, so that the dancer at Chidambaram is head and teacher of them all; it can also suggest Murugan. Who speaks the 'I am' is not fixed by the syntax.

2759.reading: With the hall as his stage, the two lights of the two feet of our Supreme who dances on it stand as his own state within the line of the five supreme nadas, and he comes himself and grants grace.
2759.nuance: ஐந்து நாதத்து ரேகை (the line of the five nadas) is unexplained. The two feet as two lights may be read as sun and moon, or as the two feet of the dance, one planted and one raised.

2760.reading: The dancing foot, the sound of its anklet, the songs sung, the many dances and the form they made: as the supreme guru celebrated them, I sought, saw them within, and so came to an end of seeking.
2760.nuance: தீர்ந்தற்றவாறு (how it ended and ceased) leaves open what ended: the search, the bonds, or the self. The dance is seen within (உளே), not in the hall.

2761.reading: As the breath rising in the heart spreads through hands, feet and the rest, so the ruby dancer in the jewelled hall, as guru, delighted in dancing everywhere.
2761.nuance: The breath pervading the limbs is the image for the dancer pervading all; குரவனாய் makes the pervading dancer also the teacher.

2762.reading: The form that dances, other than the guru's form, that form-formless is the formless one itself; she who shines as Tripura is Uma, who is form and formless.
2762.nuance: குனிக்கும் (bending) is a verb for dancing. The verse seems to distinguish the dancing form seen in the guru from the formless, and to make Uma as Tripura both; the logic is compressed.

2763.reading: The holy way is in the small hall, in the form that dances within the guru's form; for those who have perceived it closely, the way by which the form becomes formless is the way of grace itself.
2763.nuance: சிற்றம்பலம் (the small hall) is Chidambaram's shrine and in this chapter also a place in the body (2770). The dance is seen within the guru's form, which makes the guru the way to it.

2764.reading: Where the life-breath rises and swells, running twelve finger-breadths, seek it: the place where our Lord of nada's end dances in delight is the holy hall itself.
2764.nuance: பன்னிரண்டு அங்குலம் (twelve finger-breadths) is the yogic measure of the breath's reach outside the body. Line 1 (நீரும் சிரிசிடை) looks corrupt.

2765.reading: As wind, cloud, lightning, rainbow and thunder shine clearly in the sky, so the six of joy and light mingle together and yet stay distinct; he stands as a form of light, hidden.
2765.nuance: The sky image says the many appear in the one space without ceasing to be many. களிஒளி ஆறும் (the six of joy and light) is not glossed and may be six centres or six powers.

2766.reading: Beyond the knowledge that examines the five beginning with fire, the eight directions, below and above, there is bliss; this is how the Lord stands and dances, for those who have passed beyond maya and great maya to see.
2766.nuance: மாயை and மாமாயை are traditionally impure and pure maya; the dance is visible only past both. The bliss is set beyond the examining mind, not as its result.

2767.reading: The dancer joins with her of rounded bangles, the dancer joins with flawless bliss, the dancer joins with flawless knowledge: the dancer and his dancing partner are above the dance.
2767.nuance: கூத்தி (the female dancer) is Shakti. கூத்ததின் மேலே (above the dance) can mean that the pair are beyond the dance they perform, or simply engaged in it.

2768.reading: I too have come to know that the Shakti who took the left side and our Father stand in dance; for all these many lives that stand with bodies, they dance, standing as the whole of them.
2768.nuance: படங்கொடு நின்ற (standing with a படம், a cloth, picture or body) is taken here of embodied lives. The dancers in each body are Siva and Shakti.

2769.reading: Shakti's form is all bliss; the matching bliss is Uma's body; Shakti's form rising as two in the embodied, the matched bliss becomes one dance.
2769.nuance: சகளம் is the state with form; இரண்டு may be Siva and Shakti, whose two blisses make one dance. The verse is compressed.

2770.reading: Gazing steadily at the space between the brows, straight from the forehead, the mantra shines out; the place where the Supreme sits as support of supports I took as Chirrambalam and joined.
2770.nuance: A practice of fixing the gaze between the brows; the yogi names that place the small hall. பற்றுக்குப் பற்றாய் may mean the support of all supports, or the one to cling to in place of every clinging.

2771.reading: The worlds becoming tattvas, Sadasiva, the seats called Sattvi and Sambhavi in the staff, the seven in the staff becoming Siva's seat: taking these, the supreme light delighted in the dance.
2771.nuance: சாத்தவி and சாம்பவி are taken as names of seats or powers, and தண்டு as the spine. The last line repeats 2749's.

2772.reading: The great flower, the lamp-light filling the hall, is good: its petals are four and a hundred; going on, there are twelve hundred; what stands is the long mandala.
2772.nuance: The lotus with its petal-counts is traditionally a centre in the body, the thousand-petalled one at the crown, but the numbers given (நாலொடு நூறு, பத்திரு நூறு) do not match a standard list and may be corrupt.

2773.reading: Seven crores of worlds, seven crores of bodies, seven crores of directions ringed by clear waves, seven crores of lingas ringed by the eight directions: these are the temple where he dances the cosmic dance.
2773.nuance: அண்டம் and பிண்டம் (worlds and bodies) are paired as macrocosm and microcosm; both are his temple.

2774.reading: Space is his body, Muyalakan lies there, the eight directions are his holy hands, the three lights are his three eyes; in the hall of the great body he dances.
2774.nuance: முயலகன் is the dwarf under the dancer's foot, traditionally taken as ignorance (ஆணவம்). The three lights are traditionally sun, moon and fire. அங்கார் and மோகாய are obscure.

2775.reading: The hall is the whole moving and unmoving world; the hall is the first Lord's feet; the hall is the region of water and fire; the hall is the five letters.
2775.nuance: The hall (அம்பலம்) is given four identities, cosmic, devotional, yogic and mantric. அப்புத்தீ மண்டலம் is commonly taken as the moon and fire regions of the yogic body.

2776.reading: Firm drums and flutes joined, sounding 'Om'; people danced crying 'the first Lord'; the good hosts who sought him, and the many goblins, sang: so it became a Pandarangam.
2776.nuance: பாண்டரங்கம் is a named dance of Siva (see 2733); here it is the whole festive scene of music and the dancing and singing of his hosts.

2777.reading: The gods in the world, the gods beyond it, and the gods within the earth ringed by the clear directions see and worship the dance in the golden hall on the lotus feet, and so reach their goal.

2778.reading: As water springs in the mouth of those who see tamarind, for all who see the joyous holy dance tears of grace drip, the faint heart melts, and the nectar of bliss in the light wells up in the heart.
2778.nuance: The simile makes the point that the effect comes from seeing alone, as the mouth waters at the sight of tamarind. அமுது here is the bliss of the vision, without the yogic sense of nectar from the head that it has elsewhere.

2779.reading: To stagger and fall is Siva's bliss; for those who have drunk, drinking more brings frenzy; the quality that comes to those who have seen the holy dance bending in the celebrated hall comes also to those who have heard of it.
2779.nuance: உண்டார்க்கு உணவுண்டால் is obscure; read here as drink upon drink, the image of intoxication for the bliss. The last line extends the dance's effect from seeing to hearing.

2780.reading: With fire, drum, rosary, noose, goad, trident, skull and knowledge, and the blue that gives both, with the woman as one half of him, he dances the great dance.
2780.nuance: The list is of what the dancer holds in his hands, as in images of the many-armed form. உபயந்தரு நீலம் (the blue that gives both) is obscure; it may be the blue throat or Uma's colour.

2781.reading: With the eleven parts of dance in order, the joined feet, the anklets, the drum held in the hand, and the long nada, Nandi danced in love of the beyond-supreme, outside and inside.
2781.nuance: ஆடல் பதினோர் உறுப்பு may be the eleven parts of dance in Tamil dance theory or the eleven dances of tradition. புறம் அகம் (outside and inside) puts the dance both in the world and in the body.

2782.reading: As the nine dance, as the sixteen dance, as the six paths of love dance with them, as in the delightful seven the seven and fifty-six dance, he danced the fifty too: the dance of bliss.
2782.nuance: The numbers are given without their members. மார்க்கங்கள் ஆறு may be the six adhvas; அன்பதும் is probably ஐம்பதும் (the fifty letters), corrupted under the influence of அன்பு in line 2.

2783.reading: As seven in the seven, rising as seven, as one in the seven, descending and settling as one, our supreme light, the true path in the seven, joined in the drama of the seven notes.
2783.nuance: ஏழிசை are the seven notes of music; the other sevens are unglossed and may be the seven centres or the seven worlds.

2784.reading: As five in the three, as three hundred and sixty, as six in the three, as the first twelve at the root, as the three lakhs at the end, he danced first in all three the dance at delusion's end.
2784.nuance: Three hundred and sixty and twelve suggest the days and months of the year, and the three may be sun, moon and fire, which would make this the dance as time; that is a guess. மோகாந்தம் (the end of delusion) parallels நாதாந்தம் and ஞானாந்தம் elsewhere in the chapter.

2785.reading: The great jewel that dwells on the crowns of the crowned gods, the pair of the Lord's flower feet, the fair jewel that rises in the hearts of those with love: he stands beyond the world.
2785.nuance: The verse plays on மணி (jewel) through all four lines: the feet are the jewel on the gods' heads and in the lovers' hearts.

2786.reading: If he who willed it dances, the worlds dance; our thought dances to the measure that he who knows dances; if he dances, the many elements dance: this is how I rejoiced seeing the dance of the fiery one.
2786.nuance: The mind is made one of the things that move with his dance, like the worlds and the elements. எரிந்தவன் (the fiery one, or one who burned) is taken as Siva of fire.

2787.reading: The ignorant say that the First danced; no one knows the First's dancing; once someone knows the First's dancing, the dancing of the First is the Shakti of grace.
2787.nuance: To say that he danced, as a past event, is the ignorant view; known rightly, the dance is his gracious power at work. The verse shares its pattern with 2796.

2788.reading: In the two states of nine and nine, as the angle of love stands at the head and dances, appearing within the Shakti that suffers, our loving Father stood and began to dance.
2788.nuance: கோணம் (angle) suggests the triangles of a drawn diagram, and the nines may be its cells or lines; the verse cannot be pinned down. துன்புறு சத்தி (the Shakti that suffers, or that brings suffering) is unclear.

2789.reading: As the tattvas dance, Sadasiva dances, the mind dances, Siva's Shakti dances, the placed world of moving and unmoving things dances and the Veda dances, the Father too danced the dance of bliss.

2790.reading: For the two to see, in the beautiful hall, as one supreme form both with form and formless, within the Shakti of holy grace, the Siddha, the blissful one, stood as a form of grace and began to dance.
2790.nuance: இருவர் (the two) are traditionally the sages Patanjali and Vyaghrapada, for whom the dance was shown at Tillai; the verse does not name them.

2791.reading: As Siva dances and Shakti dances, as the ruin in the world dances, as the sky that does not dance dances, as the nine tattvas and nada's end dance, Siva dances within Vedanta-Siddhanta.
2791.nuance: வேதாந்தச் சித்தாந்தம் joins the two systems as the place of the dance, a pairing Tirumular makes elsewhere. நவமான may be nine or new. அவம் (ruin, waste) dances too: the dance takes in what is harmful.

2792.reading: The end of nada, the end of the four knowledges, the end of the Veda, the true bliss of Siva: in the good bliss of Sadasiva, free of elements, the Nada-Brahman is Siva's dance.
2792.nuance: நாற்போதம் (the four knowledges) and தாதற்ற (without dhatu, element or root) are not fixed. நாதப் பிரமம் (sound as Brahman) is identified with the dance.

2793.reading: So that the struggle of the five beginning with Siva ends, and pasu and pasa stand apart there in austerity, the Supreme who is austerity dances, being himself everywhere: it is the dance of knowledge of those in Siva's bliss.
2793.nuance: சிவமாதி ஐவர் (the five beginning with Siva) are commonly taken as the five lords who govern the five acts. தனித்து (standing apart) may mean that soul and bonds are separated. தவம் is repeated in every line and seems to name both practice and the Lord.

2794.reading: Standing together with the gods of time, standing for release, standing to be sought under the name Vikirta, standing so that the three bright lights dance: this is how he took me as his own.
2794.nuance: Lines 1 and 2 are obscure; விகிர்தா (the one who is other, unlike all) is a Tevaram name of Siva. The three lights are traditionally sun, moon and fire.

2795.reading: Passing beyond nada-tattva and trusting the first scripture, they found bliss shining in the elements themselves; he wove together the 'not that' and its negation so that they are not divided.
2795.nuance: நேதத்துவம் and நேதி echo the Upanishadic 'neti' (not this). The verse may mean that the way of negation and what it negates are held together by him, so that those beyond nada find bliss in the elements too; this is an interpretation of compressed lines.

2796.reading: The ignorant say 'bliss, bliss'; no one knows the great dance of bliss; once someone knows the great dance of bliss, the place where the self comes to an end is bliss.
2796.nuance: The last line puns on ஆனந்தம்: தான் அந்தம் அற்று (the self's end gone, or the self ended) is heard inside the word. Bliss is not a thing to name but the ending of the self in the dance.

2797.reading: The hand that shook off, saying 'Si', the flower hand that embraced the ascetics, saying 'Va', the golden hand set fittingly as 'A', and the fire: the holy state is 'Ma'.
2797.nuance: The dancer's hands are read as syllables of the five-letter mantra: the drum-hand or the shaking hand as சி, the embracing hand as வா, the protecting hand as அ (perhaps ய), and fire or the foot as ம. The exact matching is traditional and the verse does not give all five clearly.

2798.reading: The drum, the outstretched sweeping arm, the water and the hand with fire, and the lotus foot that trod on the embryo: in this form, recite 'Sivayanama'.
2798.nuance: Again the dancer's form spells the mantra. கருவின் மிதித்த (that trod on the embryo, or on birth) is taken as the foot crushing rebirth, or as the foot on Muyalakan; அப்பு (water) may be the Ganga in his hair.

2799.reading: Hara's drum is creation; the setting hand is preservation; Hara's fire is destruction; the pressing foot on which he rests is concealment; Hara's raised foot is grace for ever.
2799.nuance: This is the classic reading of the dancer's body as the five acts. அமைத்தல் and உற்று அணைப்பு are taken as the reassuring hand and the planted foot by tradition; the verse names the drum, fire and foot plainly.

2800.reading: The fierce one's light, the shining light, the inner light: she of tender eyes who saw the Dancer, as the first of the three murtis went between, looked on and sang the Vedas.
2800.nuance: The tender-eyed one is most likely Uma watching the dance, as in 2732; இடைசெல்ல (going between) is obscure.

2801.reading: How can I speak of Nandi, my Father, the Lord of knowledge, the beautiful dancer beyond and beyond the inner sky, reached by dwelling in the one mantra and passing beyond it?
2801.nuance: The mantra is the way in and must then be passed beyond: மருவி அது கடந்து.

2802.reading: No one knows the body to be examined of the guru Nandi in the holy hall; red like fire with white, such is the body in which one may take refuge.
2802.nuance: சீய is obscure. Red and white together may be Siva and Shakti, or nada and bindu, as in 1929; the verse gives the colours without a key.

2803.reading: Shakti, who is himself, stands as the Tatpara; she gives will to the Supreme who is himself and to souls; she conducts the distinctions beginning with knowledge; when she dances and grants grace, souls come to love Hara's feet.
2803.nuance: Shakti is made the source of will (இச்சை) both in the Lord and in souls, and the dancer of the grace that turns souls to his feet. The subject of the last line is supplied.

links.note: Both use liquor to measure an intoxication that comes without drinking. The Kural says brewed liquor delights only those who drink it, while love delights those who merely see; Tirumular says the frenzy of Siva's bliss comes to those who saw the dance and even to those who only heard of it.

Both put a dancer inside the body. The Naladiyar's dancer is the soul in its skin bag, and once it leaves, the body does not matter; Tirumular's dancers in every embodied life are Siva and Shakti themselves.

The Kural says only those who reach the Lord's feet cross the sea of births; Tirumular uses the same 'reaching the feet' to define the devotee, and makes the feet those of the dancer seen in the golden hall.
1726 says the human body's form is Chidambaram and the holy dance; 2770 locates the small hall at one point in it, the space between the brows reached by fixed gaze.
919 says the five letters are seated as the temple; 2775 says the hall of the dance is the five letters. Both make the mantra the shrine.

Two verses of nearly the same shape: the dancing foot, the sound that rises with it and the songs, and then 'this is how I saw'. 2317 sees them within the nadi; 2760 sees them within at the guru's word and ends the search there.
2727 says the five dances are the five acts; 2799 assigns each act to a part of the dancer: drum, hand, fire and the two feet.
Both map the body's three channels onto the land, with Meru and Tillai as the central channel and the Himalaya and Lanka at the sides; 2754 states the matching more plainly.
2797 reads the dancer's hands as syllables; 2798 adds the foot and tells the reader to recite சிவாயநம in that form.
The same four-line pattern: what the ignorant say, that no one knows the dance, and what the dance is once known. In 2787 it is the Shakti of grace; in 2796 it is the end of the self.
2778 says seeing the dance works as the sight of tamarind does on the mouth; 2779 extends the effect from seeing to hearing.

source_issues: 2726 lines 2 and 3 (சமயக் களியார் பரமும் கருதுறை யந்தக்) are broken in syntax and may be corrupt.
2728: தாகாண்ட and several of the -அண்டம் compounds are obscure.
2733 lines 2 and 3 (நடம் எட்டோ டு ஐந்துஆறு, திடம்உற்று ஏழும்) are unclear.
2736: ஆன்நந்தி and கான்நந்தி are obscure and may be corrupt for forms of ஆனந்தம்.
2750: the compounds குரானந்த and புரானந்த are unclear.
2754 lines 3 and 4 (கைகண்ட மூலம், படர்பொன்றி) are obscure.
2772: the petal counts do not match a standard scheme and may be corrupt.
2782: அன்பதும் is probably a corruption of ஐம்பதும்.
